territorial_scope.description: Applies to controllers that conduct business in Colorado or intentionally target commercial products or services to Colorado residents, and to controllers handling any amount of biometric identifiers.

evidence.quote: Conducts business in Colorado or produces or delivers commercial products or services that are intentionally targeted to residents of Colorado

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends the Colorado Privacy Act to regulate controllers and processors that collect, use, retain, disclose or protect biometric identifiers and data, including written policies, consent, sale and disclosure limits, and employer consent rules. Takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to a referendum petition.
summary.long: Adds C.R.S. 6-1-1314 to the Colorado Privacy Act, with new biometric definitions in 6-1-1303 and an applicability rule in 6-1-1304. Controllers must adopt a public written policy with a retention schedule and deletion dates and a security-incident protocol; processors need an incident protocol. Before collecting biometric identifiers, controllers must give notice and obtain consent. They may not sell, lease or trade identifiers, disclose them except in listed cases, or refuse service or vary prices for consumers who decline or exercise rights. Consumers may request free access to their biometric data details. Employers may require consent only for listed security, timekeeping and safety purposes, and may not retaliate. The Department of Law may adopt rules. The act reaches controllers handling any amount of biometric identifiers and takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to a referendum petition. The text contains no penalty provisions; its title refers to remedies and civil actions, which do not appear in this document.

notes: Text is the enrolled bill; strike-through and underline markings were not reliably preserved, so the operative wording of amended 6-1-1304(1) is partly mixed with deleted text (artifacts such as '(-b)', '(0' and '(II)'). Capitalised text is read as new material. Section 2 adds 6-1-1314 as a new section rather than amending an existing one. Section 3 new 6-1-1303(2.4) ends with an incomplete list (an 'OR' after item (d) and an empty item (e)). Section 5 sets the effective date at July 1, 2025, subject to a referendum petition. The text gives no approval date (signature dates are illegible). Relations and entities are present, so the section_status entries record only that nothing is missing.

obligations.summary: Controller that controls or processes biometric identifiers must adopt a written policy that establishes a retention schedule, includes a protocol for responding to data security incidents (including consumer breach notice under 6-1-716), and includes deletion guidelines.
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))
obligations.conditional_on: Controller controls or processes one or more biometric identifiers

evidence.quote: A CONTROLLER THAT CONTROLS OR PROCESSES ONE OR MORE BIOMETRIC IDENTIFIERS SHALL ADOPT A WRITTEN POLICY THAT

obligations.summary: The written policy must include guidelines requiring deletion of a biometric identifier on or before the earliest of: purpose satisfied; 24 months after last interaction with the consumer; or the earliest reasonably feasible date, no more than 45 days after the controller determines storage is no longer necessary (extendable by up to 45 additional days), with an annual review.
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))
obligations.conditional_on: Controller controls or processes one or more biometric identifiers

obligations.summary: Controller must make its written policy available to the public, except policies applying only to current employees, policies used solely internally by employees and agents, and the internal security-incident protocol.
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))

obligations.summary: Processor of biometric identifiers or biometric data must have a protocol for responding to data security incidents, including a process for notifying the controller of a breach under 6-1-716.

obligations.summary: Before collecting or processing a consumer's biometric identifier, the controller must satisfy the duties in 6-1-1308 and inform the consumer (or legally authorized representative) clearly that the identifier is being collected, of the specific purpose and retention length, and whether it will be disclosed to a processor and for what purpose.
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))
obligations.conditional_on: Controller collects or processes a consumer's biometric identifier

obligations.summary: Controller processing a consumer's biometric identifier shall not sell, lease or trade it, nor disclose, redisclose or disseminate it, except with consent, for completing a financial transaction requested by the consumer, to a processor for the collection purpose, or where required by state or federal law.
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))

obligations.summary: Controller shall not refuse goods or services based on a consumer's refusal to consent to biometric processing unless necessary to provide the good or service; shall not charge a different price or provide a different quality to consumers exercising rights under part 13; and shall not purchase a biometric identifier unless it pays the consumer, the purchase is unrelated to providing a product or service, and consent was obtained.
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))

obligations.summary: Controller or processor shall store, transmit and protect from disclosure all biometric identifiers using the standard of care within the controller's industry and in accordance with C.R.S. 6-1-1305(4) and 6-1-1308(5).
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))

obligations.summary: On request of a consumer or legally authorized representative, a controller that collects biometric data must disclose free of charge the category or description of the data and the source, purpose, third parties disclosed to and purposes, and categories disclosed to third parties. Applies only to listed entities (business in Colorado, collecting biometric data, and meeting personal data volume or revenue tests) and to common-branded affiliates and certain two-business joint ventures.

obligations.summary: Employer may require, as a condition of employment, that an employee or prospective employee consent to collection and processing of biometric identifiers only for permitting access to secure locations and hardware/software, recording the workday (including breaks over 30 minutes), workplace or employee safety and security, or public safety in an emergency. Consent may not be sought to retain data used for current employee location tracking or time-on-application tracking.
obligations.applies_from: Act takes effect July 1, 2025, subject to referendum petition (Sec. 5(1)); applies to collection and processing on and after the effective date (Sec. 5(2))

obligations.summary: Employer may not require consent to biometric collection or processing for uses other than those in subsection (6)(a) as a condition of employment, nor retaliate against an employee or prospective employee who does not consent; such other uses are permitted only with consent (subsection (6)(b)).

enforcement.note: The supplied text contains no penalty, fine, sanction, remedy or civil-action provision. The heading of new C.R.S. 6-1-1314 lists "remedies and civil actions", but no such subsection is reproduced in the document. Subsection (7) only authorises the Department of Law to promulgate rules.
